The national template raster in a NAT_DATA folder

Source: R/natdata.R
natdata_template.Rd

Opens the national 1 km template raster of a NAT_DATA folder (ConsTech's shared national data), the grid every NAT_DATA layer is on. It is the one place the template's location in NAT_DATA is written down: pass the SpatRaster it returns as the template of rasterize_aoi(), align_raster(), read_rij_matrix(), clip_rij_matrix() and extract_layers().

Usage

natdata_template(natdata_dir, file = "_1km/idx.tif")

Arguments

natdata_dir

The NAT_DATA folder: a single path to an existing folder, such as a dated release (NAT_DATA_20261009). Where NAT_DATA lives is each tool's own setting; this function only reads from it.

file

The template's file within natdata_dir, as a path relative to it. The default, "_1km/idx.tif", is NAT_DATA's convention, where wtw-data-prep2 and the opportunity-screening-toolkit read it.

Value

A SpatRaster with one layer, read from file.path(natdata_dir, file). Nothing is written.

Method

Nothing is computed: the file is opened with terra::rast(), which reads its header and leaves its values on disk until they are needed, so a national template is not loaded into memory. It must have one layer and a coordinate reference system. In NAT_DATA, _1km/idx.tif is the national grid of 1 km cells in Canada_Albers_WGS_1984, holding each cell's national number (numbered row by row from the bottom-left cell) and NA where there is no data. constechr functions use the template's grid and which of its cells have data, and rasterize_aoi() with value = "template" its values.

See also

Other natdata: create_1km_grid(), read_natdata_metadata()

Examples

# A small NAT_DATA-like folder: its _1km/idx.tif is a 10 x 10 template
natdata_dir <- system.file("extdata", "natdata", package = "constechr")
template <- natdata_template(natdata_dir)
template
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 10, 10, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 1000, 1000  (x, y)
#> extent      : 1000000, 1010000, 600000, 610000  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#> source      : idx.tif
#> name        : index
#> min value   :     3
#> max value   :   100

# The AOI's cells on the national template
aoi <- system.file("extdata", "aoi.gpkg", package = "constechr")
rasterize_aoi(aoi, template, cells = "touches")
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 3, 3, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 1000, 1000  (x, y)
#> extent      : 1003000, 1006000, 604000, 607000  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#> source(s)   : memory
#> varname     : idx
#> name        : index
#> min value   :    34
#> max value   :    56
